clinician.final_diagnosis: Cytomegalovirus retinitis with a macular star in an immunocompetent individual.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 40-year-old immunocompetent man presented with diminished vision in his right eye following trauma, attributed to a traumatic cataract. After cataract surgery, the fundus examination was initially reported as normal. Subsequent workup for persistent symptoms revealed elevated CMV IgG titers (1073 AU/ml) and a normal CD4 count (950 cells/mm3), while other infectious and autoimmune markers were negative. Initial treatment with prednisolone and Septran DS was ineffective. Following this, valganciclovir therapy was initiated. 1.5 months after starting valganciclovir, the patient's vision improved, and fundus examination showed a healing choroiditis patch with a resolving hemorrhagic patch and macular star. Repeated serology showed a decrease in CMV IgG titer (from 1073 AU/ml to 159 AU/ml).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with diminished vision in right eye after trauma and had a traumatic cataract.
Patient was immunocompetent with a normal CD4 cell count (950 cells/mm3).
Elevated CMV IgG titer (1073 AU/ml) was detected.
Initial treatment with prednisolone and Septran DS did not result in improvement.
After 1.5 months of valganciclovir therapy, vision improved to 6/6, and fundus examination showed a healing choroiditis patch with a resolving hemorrhagic patch and macular star.
CMV IgG titer decreased to 159 AU/ml after 1.5 months of treatment.
